"""A document-onset pulse, with a lexical estimate of its size.

The main signal is confined to the first token, or an uninterrupted repetition
of that token. Its size is estimated from spelling, word class and a few broad
WordNet meanings. These are approximate lexical tendencies, not a word lookup;
token-specific variation and small later activations are left unexplained.
"""
import re
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
AUXILIARIES = frozenset((
    'be am is are was were been being have has had having '
    'do does did done will would shall should can could may might must'
).split())
PRONOUNS = frozenset((
    'i me my mine myself we us our ours ourselves you your yours '
    'yourself yourselves he him his himself she her hers herself it its itself '
    'they them their theirs themselves this that these those who whom whose '
    'what which whoever whatever someone anyone everyone nobody'
).split())
MEANING_ADJUSTMENTS = {
    'noun.cognition': 1.39,
    'noun.group': 1.61,
    'noun.possession': 2.18,
    'verb.change': -1.00,
}


def onset_size(text):
    if text.startswith('<|'):
        return 1.75
    word = text.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    # C/JSON-style escaped characters are a stronger kind of onset.
    if len(word) > 1 and word[0] == '\\' and word[1] in 'nt\"\'':
        return 11.5

    value = 1.33 + 0.445 * min(len(word), 15)
    value += 1.71 * word.islower() + 1.46 * word.isupper()
    value += 3.09 * word.isdigit()
    if not word and len(text) > 1 and '\n' not in text:
        value += 2.88
    if word and not any(ch.isalnum() for ch in word):
        value += 1.32
    if word.startswith('.'):
        value -= 1.73
    if word.startswith(','):
        value -= 1.68

    if re.fullmatch('[A-Za-z]+', word):
        pos = wordnet.parts_of_speech(lower)
        categories = wordnet.categories(lower)
        frequency = max(0.0, zipf_frequency(lower, 'en') - 2.0)
        if text.startswith(' '):
            value += 2.48 * bool(pos) - 0.314 * frequency
        if 'adverb' in pos:
            value -= 0.427 * frequency
        value += sum(weight for category, weight in MEANING_ADJUSTMENTS.items()
                     if category in categories)
        value -= 2.57 * (lower in AUXILIARIES)
        value -= 2.13 * (lower == 'to')
        value += 2.44 * lower.endswith('tion')
        value += 1.02 * (lower in PRONOUNS)
    return float(value)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    start = (prefix.position == 0 or
             prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2])
    token = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    if start:
        value = onset_size(prefix.token_strings[-1])
        return (token, value), value
    if carry is not None and token == carry[0]:
        return carry, carry[1]
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5120 fires on the first token of each document.

A document's first token has no earlier text in its attention window, so this
component's activation there depends only on which word that token is. Everywhere
else it is near zero, so the program predicts 0 except at document starts.

At a document start the predicted value follows the word's kind:
  - English content words are high, and higher for nouns (about 11-12 for a
    spaced noun, with a noun suffix such as -tion, -ity, -ment or a plural -s).
    Longer words score higher.
  - Verbs, code keywords and modal/auxiliary verbs are low (about 1).
  - Function words are middling-low (about 2.5).
  - Capitalised words are about 3.5 (no leading space) or 5.5 (leading space).
  - Digits are about 5; non-Latin text about 3.5.
  - Spaces, newlines, punctuation and special tokens are low (about 1.5).

Main program: `step` detects a document start (the first token of the row, or
a change of document id) and returns `start_value` of that token's text."""
import re

READS = ()

FUNCTION_WORDS = set("""a an the and or but if then else so as of to in on at by for from with without
into onto over under about above below between through during before after is are was were be been
being am do does did have has had it its this that these those there here he she they we you i me him
her us them my your his our their not no nor can could will would shall should may might must just also
too very more most some any all each every both either neither one only own same such than which who
whom whose what when where why how while because until against up down out off again further once""".split())
CODE_WORDS = set("""import from def class return elif while try catch throw using async await typedef
instanceof typeof enumerate private public static void new null none true false self print""".split())
NOUNS = set("""time year people way day man thing woman life child world school state family student group
country problem hand part place case week company system program question work government number night
point home water room mother area money story fact month lot right study book eye job word business
issue side kind head house service friend father power hour game line end member law car city
community name president team minute idea kid body information back parent face others level office
door health person art war history party result change morning reason research girl guy moment air
teacher force education foot boy age policy process music market sense nation plan college interest
death experience effect class control care field development role effort rate heart drug leader light
voice wife police mind price report decision son view relationship town road arm difference value
building action model season society tax director position player record paper space ground form event
official matter center couple site project activity star table court oil situation cost industry figure
street image phone data picture practice piece land product doctor wall patient worker news test movie
love support technology step baby computer type attention film tree source organization hair look""".split())
VERBS = set("""make get use go see know take come want need find give tell work call try ask feel become
leave put mean keep let begin seem help talk turn start show hear play run move like live believe bring
happen write provide sit stand lose pay meet include continue set learn change lead understand watch
follow stop create speak read allow add spend grow open walk win offer remember consider appear buy wait
serve die send expect build stay fall cut reach kill remain""".split())
NOUN_SUFFIXES = ("tion", "sion", "ment", "ity", "ness", "ance", "ence", "ism", "ics", "ogy", "ure", "ies")
VERB_SUFFIXES = ("ing", "ed", "ly", "al", "ic", "ize", "ate", "en", "ous", "ive", "ful", "able", "ible")


def start_value(token):
    """Activation predicted for a token that begins a document."""
    word = token.strip()
    if not word or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z]+", word):
        if word.isdigit():
            return 5.0
        if any(ord(ch) > 127 for ch in word):
            return 3.5
        return 1.5                      # spaces, newlines, punctuation, special tokens
    if word[0].isupper():
        return 5.5 if token.startswith(" ") else 3.5
    w = word.lower()
    if w in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return 2.5
    if w in CODE_WORDS or w in VERBS:
        return 1.0
    value = 0.6 * len(w)
    if w in NOUNS or w.endswith(NOUN_SUFFIXES):
        value += 4.0
    elif w.endswith("s") and not w.endswith("ss"):
        value += 3.0
    elif w.endswith(VERB_SUFFIXES):
        value += 0.0
    else:
        value += 1.0
    return value + (1.0 if token.startswith(" ") else 0.0)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    starts_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not starts_doc:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, start_value(prefix.token_strings[-1])

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5121 -- the English preposition "on".

What it does: it reads the word "on" in the residual stream and is silent on
almost everything else. It fires on "on" and "upon" in any case, with or
without a leading space (" on", "On", " ON", "upon"), at strength about 1.

Two refinements, both read from the same token:
  * "on" right after a word that takes "on" as a fixed complement ("based on",
    "depending on", "depends on", "dependent on", "focus on", "rely on",
    "impact on", "effect on", "and so on") is weaker, about 0.3.
  * Short word pieces that end in "on", as inside "taxon", "Xeon", "Anton",
    "pseudonym", fire at about half strength. Common words that end in "on"
    but do not fire ("one", "con", "ton", "mon", "ion", "non", "don", "son",
    "only", "long") are excluded.

It is stateless: it looks only at the newest token and the one before it.
"""

READS = ()

ON_WORDS = {"on", "upon"}
WEAK_BEFORE_ON = {
    "based", "depending", "depends", "depend", "dependent",
    "focus", "focused", "focusing", "rely", "relies", "relying",
    "so", "impact", "effect",
}
NOT_ON_PIECES = {"one", "con", "ton", "mon", "ion", "non", "don", "son", "only", "long"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    if word in ON_WORDS:
        return carry, (0.3 if before in WEAK_BEFORE_ON else 1.0)
    if word.endswith("on") and len(word) <= 4 and word not in NOT_ON_PIECES:
        return carry, 0.5
    return carry, 0.0

"""A conservative predictor for spelling fragments and document starts.

Track up to six short pieces of an unspaced word. Dense mixed capitalization,
interleaved letters/digits, and Latin phonetic spelling give small negative
predictions. Ignore long encoded-looking and hexadecimal runs. Repeated
interpuncts and a few document-initial numeral/punctuation patterns have
separate, larger responses measured in training. Other values stay near zero;
this leaves most small, token-specific fluctuations unexplained.
"""
import regex

READS = ()
LATIN = regex.compile(r'\p{Script=Latin}+\Z')
PHONETIC = regex.compile(r'[\p{Block=IPA_Extensions}ð]')
HEX = regex.compile(r'[0-9A-Fa-f]+\Z')
ASCII_RUN = regex.compile(r'[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+\Z')
PIECE = regex.compile(
    r'[\p{Script=Latin}\p{Block=Spacing_Modifier_Letters}0-9]+\Z'
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, (), 0, 0)
    recent, run_length, position = carry[1:]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    q = token.strip()
    if not token or token[0].isspace() or not ASCII_RUN.fullmatch(q):
        run_length = 0
    if ASCII_RUN.fullmatch(q):
        run_length += len(q)
    if not token or token[0].isspace() or len(q) > 3:
        recent = ()
    if q and len(q) <= 3 and PIECE.fullmatch(q):
        recent = (recent + (q,))[-6:]
    else:
        recent = ()

    value = -0.001
    word = ''.join(recent)
    if len(q) >= 2 and set(q) == {'·'}:
        value = -0.994
    elif position == 0 and token == '//\n':
        value = -2.669
    elif (position == 1 and token == ' *'
          and prefix.token_strings[-2] in ('/*\n', '/*\r\n')):
        value = -0.85
    elif position == 0 and token == ' .':
        value = -1.763
    elif (position == 1 and token == '2'
          and prefix.token_strings[-2] == '1'):
        value = -1.823
    elif position == 0 and q.isascii() and q.isdigit():
        value = -0.218
    elif (len(recent) >= 2 and run_length <= 18
          and not HEX.fullmatch(word)):
        letters = sum(c.isalpha() for c in word)
        case = number = 0
        for a, b in zip(word, word[1:]):
            case += (a.isalpha() and b.isalpha()
                     and a.isupper() != b.isupper())
            number += ((a.isalpha() and b.isdigit())
                       or (a.isdigit() and b.isalpha()))
        # An initial capital followed by lowercase is ordinary capitalization.
        if len(word) > 1 and word[0].isupper() and word[1].islower():
            case = max(case - 1, 0)
        short = (4 - len(q)) / 3
        latin = bool(LATIN.fullmatch(q))
        if len(word) / len(recent) <= 2:
            title_pieces = sum(len(s) > 1 and s.istitle() for s in recent)
            short_camel = (len(q) > 1 and q.istitle()) or title_pieces >= 2
            if (latin and short_camel and letters >= 3
                    and case / (letters - 1) >= .5):
                value -= .04 * max(case - 1, 0) * short
            if (word.islower() and letters >= 2
                    and number / max(len(word) - 1, 1) >= .7):
                weight = 1 if latin else .25
                value -= .025 * max(number - 1, 0) * short * weight
        if latin and PHONETIC.search(word):
            value -= .05 * min(len(recent) - 1, 5) * short
    return (doc, recent, run_length, position + 1), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5122 - a mostly-quiet component with three readable negative cases.

Its activation is near zero almost everywhere (typical size 0.03-0.05) and its sign on
ordinary text is not predictable from any simple feature we could find. What it does do,
reliably and strongly, is go negative in three situations:

1. Middle-dot leaders ("··"). If a document opens with a run of "··" tokens (nothing else
   before them), the activation sits at about -1 for the whole run. A "··" that comes after
   other text gives only a weak negative (about -0.1).
2. A bare number as the first token of a document (digits "0".."9" at position 0) gives
   about -0.2.
3. Random-looking alphanumeric codes, where letters and digits alternate character by
   character (r3f3r3nc, 4n3e2vE1, 5w4n3e2). When the last six characters switch between
   letter and digit at least five times, the value is about -0.2. Real values there range
   from about 0 to -2, so this is a weak prediction.

Everything else is predicted as 0.
"""

READS = ()

DOT_LEADER = "··"
FLIP_WINDOW = 6  # characters of recent text inspected for letter/digit alternation
MIN_FLIPS = 5  # letter<->digit switches needed inside that window

DOC_START_VALUE = -0.2
DOT_RUN_VALUE = -1.0
MID_TEXT_DOT_VALUE = -0.1
CODE_RUN_VALUE = -0.2


def _char_kind(ch):
    if ch.isascii() and ch.isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if ch.isascii() and ch.isalpha():
        return "letter"
    return "other"


def _alternation_count(text):
    kinds = [_char_kind(ch) for ch in text[-FLIP_WINDOW:]]
    flips = 0
    for before, after in zip(kinds, kinds[1:]):
        if before != after and "other" not in (before, after):
            flips += 1
    return flips, "digit" in kinds and "letter" in kinds


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_document = (
        len(prefix.document_ids) == 1
        or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    if carry is None or new_document:
        # Fresh document: no tokens seen yet, and the run of dot leaders is empty.
        offset, recent, all_dots = 0, "", True
    else:
        offset, recent, all_dots = carry

    all_dots = all_dots and token == DOT_LEADER
    if token == DOT_LEADER:
        value = DOT_RUN_VALUE if all_dots else MID_TEXT_DOT_VALUE
    elif offset == 0 and token.isascii() and token.isdigit():
        value = DOC_START_VALUE
    else:
        flips, mixed = _alternation_count(recent + token)
        in_code = flips >= MIN_FLIPS and mixed and _char_kind(token[-1:]) != "other"
        value = CODE_RUN_VALUE if in_code else 0.0

    carry = (offset + 1, (recent + token)[-FLIP_WINDOW:], all_dots)
    return carry, float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5123 as a set of readable token-pattern rules.

The component is sparse and idiosyncratic. Its activation is high on a handful of
recognisable patterns and near zero elsewhere, so this program predicts those patterns
and predicts 0 everywhere else:

  * printf-style conversion letters right after "%" (the "d" in "%d", "s" in "%s"): strong
  * clock times: the colon after a 1-2 digit hour (0-23), as in "15:04": moderate
  * month and date marks: "月" after a digit ("12月"), "/" after a digit ("10/05"): moderate
  * escaped and encoded text: hex byte escapes ("\\xe2" and its pieces), "&#" HTML
    entities, escaped quotes "\\'", mojibake "â", NUL bytes (UTF-16-style text): strong
  * the double-underscore token "__" (Python dunders such as __init__): strong
  * GitHub URLs: the ".com" right after "github" ("github.com/owner/repo"): strongly negative
  * file-extension dots ".go", ".rs", ".io", ".net": weakly negative
  * the first token of a document, when it is a code keyword ("package", "class", "def"):
    positive

Each prediction uses only the current token, the one before it, and the document start.
"""
READS = ()

DIGITS = tuple("0123456789")
CODE_START = {
    "class", "def", "const", "package", "import", "using", "let", "int", "str",
    "function", "var", "#include", "#!/", "//\n", "#ifndef", "public", "from", "use", "fn",
}
ESCAPES = {"&#", "\\'", "xe", "xc", "xa", "â"}


def _hour_before(strs):
    """True if the digits just before this colon form an hour (0-23) on their own."""
    digits = ""
    i = len(strs) - 2
    while i >= 0 and strs[i] in DIGITS and len(digits) < 3:
        digits = strs[i] + digits
        i -= 1
    if not 1 <= len(digits) <= 2 or int(digits) > 23:
        return False
    return i < 0 or strs[i] not in DIGITS


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strs = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    tok = strs[-1]
    prev = strs[-2] if len(strs) > 1 else ""

    # first token of a document: only its identity is known, so use code keywords
    if len(strs) == 1 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        return None, (1.3 if tok.strip() in CODE_START else 0.0)

    if tok == ".com" and "hub" in prev:
        return None, -3.3
    if len(tok) == 1 and tok.isascii() and tok.isalpha() and prev.endswith("%"):
        return None, 1.7
    if tok in ("\x00", "__"):
        return None, 1.1
    if tok == "月" and prev in DIGITS:
        return None, 1.6
    if tok in ESCAPES or tok.startswith("\\x"):
        return None, 1.0
    if tok == ":" and _hour_before(strs):
        return None, 0.5
    if tok == "/" and prev in DIGITS:
        return None, 0.3
    if tok in (".go", ".rs", ".io", ".net"):
        return None, -0.3
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5124 -- a "nu" spelling detector, plus German "nehmen/kommen" stems.

What it responds to, in plain terms:

* Strongly NEGATIVE on the sound "nu" just typed. Activation is largest (about -4) when "nu"
  is a whole token ("nu", " nu", "gnu") or when the "u" completes an "n|u" split across two
  tokens. Other scripts spelling the same sound count too: ну, ню (Cyrillic), ヌ, ニュ, 뉴, 누.
  Right after "nu" the next letter matters: nut, nun, nuance, nuts, nuisance are strongly
  negative, while num, nue and nur are weak.
* POSITIVE on the German verb stems of nehmen (take) and kommen (come) as they end a word:
  nehmen, übernommen, aufgenommen, nahme, Übernahme, nimmt (about +5 for full forms),
  stems such as nahm, nehm, nah, nahe (about +3.4), and -ommen (about +2).
* A small positive value on the colon of a "Title:" label (about +2).
* Everything else predicts 0.

Why: this component is a letter-level feature in the first MLP. It reads the spelling of the
text just written (only the last few characters, across token boundaries), not word meaning.
The rules below are the simplest readable description that captures most of its variance.
"""

READS = ()

# The sound "nu", as it is spelled in several scripts. Value: activation when it is the last thing
# typed as a whole token ("nu", "u" completing "n|u"); scaled for other token shapes below.
NU_SOUNDS = {
    "nu": -2.6,
    "nú": -4.0,
    "nü": -2.0,
    "ну": -1.3,
    "ню": -2.4,
    "ヌ": -4.0,
    "ニュ": -3.5,
    "뉴": -3.9,
    "누": -1.4,
    "µν": -6.0,  # the Greek letter nu after mu, as in physics formulas
}

# Endings of the German verb stems nehmen / kommen (and their forms).
TAKE_COME = {
    "nehmen": 5.0,
    "nahmen": 5.0,
    "nommen": 5.0,
    "nemen": 5.0,
    "nimmt": 5.0,
    "nahme": 5.0,
    "nahe": 3.4,
    "nehm": 3.4,
    "nahm": 3.4,
    "nimm": 3.4,
    "nomm": 3.4,
    "hme": 3.4,
    "neh": 3.4,
    "nah": 3.4,
    "ommen": 2.0,
}

# Letters that, once they follow "nu", keep the activation strong (nut, nun, nuance...).
STRONG_AFTER_NU = "kcbjfvytldi"
MEDIUM_AFTER_NU = "nagosx"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    # The text typed so far in this document, up to the last 8 characters (lowercased).
    first = t
    while first > 0 and docs[first - 1] == docs[t] and t - first < 3:
        first -= 1
    text = "".join(prefix.token_strings[first:]).lower()[-8:]
    current = prefix.token_strings[t].strip().lower()

    for sound, value in NU_SOUNDS.items():
        if text.endswith(sound):
            # "nu" as a whole token, or the "u" of a split "n|u", is the strongest case.
            if current in ("nu", "u"):
                return None, value * 1.6
            return None, value * 0.6
        if text[:-1].endswith(sound):
            # One letter after "nu": depends on which letter it is.
            if text[-1] in STRONG_AFTER_NU:
                return None, value
            if text[-1] in MEDIUM_AFTER_NU:
                return None, value * 0.4
            return None, value * 0.1

    for stem, value in TAKE_COME.items():
        if text.endswith(stem):
            return None, value

    if text.endswith(("nam", "nem", "nim", "nom")):
        return None, 0.5
    if text.endswith("title:"):
        return None, 2.2
    return None, 0.0

"""Approximate the negative response to short long-a and related vowel spellings.

Doubled a/A may straddle token boundaries. Unicode names identify related
vowel forms, after joining UTF-8 fragments. Frequent-word spellings are
weakened, with a smaller response on short within-word continuations.
Amplitudes are conservative: spelling is only a hint, not a reliable trigger.
Other positions receive a small baseline, larger at document starts.
"""
import codecs
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()


@lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def common_word(piece):
    languages = ('nl', 'fi', 'da', 'de', 'fr', 'ro', 'vi')
    return max(zipf_frequency(piece, lang) for lang in languages) >= 4.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    _, pending, previous, last_strength = (doc, b'', '', 0.) if first else carry
    raw = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    text = raw.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    decoded, used = codecs.utf_8_decode(pending + raw, 'replace', False)
    pending = (pending + raw)[used:]
    piece, complete = text.strip(), decoded.strip()
    strength = 0.
    if 'aa' in piece.lower() and len(piece) <= 4:
        strength += 2.5 if piece.startswith('Aa') else 1.1
    if len(piece) <= 3:
        if any(ch in piece for ch in 'âÂ'):
            strength += 1.2
        if any(ch in piece for ch in 'āĀ'):
            strength += 1.6
    if strength and piece.isalpha() and not piece.isupper():
        if common_word(piece):
            strength *= 0.2
    if previous.lower().endswith('a') and text.lower().startswith('a'):
        strength += 1.4 if len(piece) <= 2 else 0.6
    if len(complete) <= 3 and 'آ' in complete:
        strength += 1.0
    if len(complete) <= 2:
        names = [unicodedata.name(ch, '') for ch in complete]
        if any('VOWEL SIGN AA' in n or n.endswith('LETTER AA') for n in names):
            strength += 2.8
        if any('GREEK' in n and 'ALPHA' in n and
               ('PSILI' in n or 'DASIA' in n) for n in names):
            strength += 1.5
    if complete == 'า':
        strength += 0.6
    if piece == 'وا' and previous.rstrip().endswith('خ'):
        strength += 0.75
    spill = 0.
    if text and not text[0].isspace() and len(piece) <= 2:
        spill = min(1.0, 0.4 * last_strength)
    value = (0.15 if first else -0.002) - min(3.6, strength + spill)
    return (doc, pending, text, strength), 0.65 * value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5125 — a document-start unit with a few negative token fragments.

What it does, in plain terms:
1. First token of each document (or of each packed row): a moderate positive value (~+0.2).
   The component has no earlier context there, and its output at that position is mostly positive.
2. Stray Latin letters from broken UTF-8 (mojibake), e.g. a lone 'â' or 'ā' that appears when
   bytes of a curly quote or a non-ASCII letter are read as Latin-1: strongly negative.
   'Â', 'Ã', 'Å' are weaker.
3. Doubled-'a' fragments inside names and acronyms ('AA', 'aa', 'AAAA', 'CAA', 'aan', 'aar'):
   negative, as in 'M|AA| Spectrum', 'Kabhi Alvida N|aa|'.
4. Arabic alef-madda 'آ' and Thai sara-aa 'า' pieces: negative.
Everything else is predicted as 0 (the component's typical small value).
Values are the average activations of each class, measured on training rows.
"""
import re

READS = ()

DOC_START = 0.22  # mean activation on a document's first token

# Lone accented Latin letters that mojibake leaves behind (value = mean activation)
STRAY_ACCENT = {"â": -1.7, "ā": -2.0, "Â": -0.7, "Ã": -0.3, "Å": -0.6, "ī": -0.4}
# Doubled-a name and acronym fragments
A_FRAGMENT = re.compile(r"^(?:[aA]{2,}|[CM]?AA[A-Z]?|aa[nrt]?)$")
ARABIC_ALEF_MADDA = {"آ": -1.2, "الآ": -1.7}
THAI_SARA_AA = {"า": -1.8, "าน": -0.9}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    s = tok.strip()
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, DOC_START
    if s in STRAY_ACCENT:
        return carry, STRAY_ACCENT[s]
    if A_FRAGMENT.match(s):
        return carry, -1.2
    if s in ARABIC_ALEF_MADDA:
        return carry, ARABIC_ALEF_MADDA[s]
    if s in THAI_SARA_AA:
        return carry, THAI_SARA_AA[s]
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5126: a "namespace" / block-opener detector.

What it responds to, in plain terms. The component switches on where source code opens a
named container, and most strongly on the word `namespace` starting a line: a top-level
declaration such as `namespace Foo {` in C#, C++ or PHP, after `using System;` or
`#include` lines (about 10 to 16). Other responses, all smaller:
- `using namespace` in C++ (about 6.5), and `namespace` in any other form (`_namespace`,
  `.namespace`, `Namespace`, about 2.6);
- at the start of a line, the opener of a top-level block: `(function` (an IIFE wrapper,
  about 7), `describe` (about 3.5), `module` (about 3.4);
- `com` or `org` right after `package` near the top of a file (`package com.x`, about 7);
- the `('` or `("` that opens a `describe(` or `suite(` test block (about 4.5);
- negative: the first token of each document, which has no earlier context (about -0.25),
  and the middle-dot token in a long run of dots (about -2).

Everything else predicts 0. The program reads only the current token, the token before
it, and the token's position in its document (carried from step to step), so it is a
short rule over the token stream. The values are rounded means of the component's
activations on training rows. They predict the activation, not its effect on the output.
Most of the component's variance is a diffuse, small, token-level noise (about 0.06
standard deviation) that no simple concept captures, so the program leaves it at 0.
"""

READS = ()

# keywords that open a top-level block when they start a line, with their typical value
BLOCK_OPENERS = {"namespace": 10.0, "(function": 7.0, "describe": 3.5, "module": 3.4}
USING_NAMESPACE = 6.5  # `using namespace`
OTHER_NAMESPACE = 2.6  # any other form of the word
PACKAGE_NAME = 7.0     # `com` / `org` right after `package` near the top of a file
TEST_BLOCK = 4.5       # `('` / `("` right after `describe` or `suite`
FIRST_TOKEN = -0.25    # the first token of a document
DOT_RUN = -2.0         # the middle-dot token, repeated in long dot leaders


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = raw.strip()
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        # first token of a document: nothing before it in this document
        pos, prev_raw, prev_word = 0, "", ""
    else:
        pos, prev_raw, prev_word = carry[1] + 1, carry[2], carry[3]
    starts_line = prev_raw.strip() == "" or prev_raw.endswith("\n")
    if starts_line and raw == word and word in BLOCK_OPENERS:
        value = BLOCK_OPENERS[word]
    elif "namespace" in word.lower():
        if word == "namespace" and prev_word == "using":
            value = USING_NAMESPACE
        else:
            value = OTHER_NAMESPACE
    elif pos == 0:
        value = FIRST_TOKEN
    elif prev_word == "package" and pos < 5 and word in ("com", "org"):
        value = PACKAGE_NAME
    elif prev_word in ("describe", "suite") and raw in ("('", '("'):
        value = TEST_BLOCK
    elif word == "··":
        value = DOT_RUN
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (doc, pos, raw, word), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5127 - a document-start detector.

What it does: this component is silent almost everywhere. It fires on the first token of
each document: the token right after an <|endoftext|> inside a packed row, or the first
token of a row. There it writes a large value that depends on what kind of token that is.
Capitalised English words and plain words get a high value, punctuation, symbols, code
fragments and non-Latin text a low one. At every other position it outputs 0.

Main idea: only the first token of a document matters, so the program tracks document
boundaries (a change of document id, or the start of the row) and reads the token kind.
"""

READS = ()

WORD_LEVEL = 7.7      # an ASCII word, with or without a leading space
CAPITAL_LEVEL = 8.0   # an ASCII word starting with a capital letter
OTHER_LEVEL = 5.3     # punctuation, symbols, whitespace, code, non-ASCII text


def token_level(piece):
    """The value at a document's first token, from the token's own text."""
    word = piece.strip()
    if not word.isascii() or not word.isalpha():
        return OTHER_LEVEL
    return CAPITAL_LEVEL if word[0].isupper() else WORD_LEVEL


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # A document starts at the row's first token, and wherever the document id changes.
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if starts_document:
        return None, token_level(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    return None, 0.0

"""Approximate the component's negative English molecular-biology signal.

Recognize biological word families, joining word fragments across tokens.
Two fading vocabulary counts provide nearby and broader biological context.
That context strengthens biological senses of expression, regulation, protein
structure and laboratory manipulations. Connecting 'of' inherits the preceding
process's signal. State resets at document boundaries.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
READS = ()

# Word family, ordinary response, additional response in biological context.
FAMILIES = (
    # Nucleic acids; genes and mutations; proteins.
    (r'[mrist]*rna|mir$|sir$|dna|nucleotid|oligonucleotid', -.29, -.86),
    (r'gene$|genes$|genet|genom|mutan|mutat|allele|chromosom|transgen', -1.14, -.20),
    (r'protein|peptid|enzym|kinase|cytokin|antigen|antibod|immunoglob', -1.35, .16),
    # Expression, regulation, and molecular processes.
    (r'express|coexpress|overexpress', -.26, -4.01),
    (r'transcript|splic|regulat|encod|upreg|downreg|silenc|target|delet', -.14, -2.00),
    (r'activat|inhibit|induc(?:e|ed|ing|tion|ible)|bind|bound$|'
     r'synthes|phosphor|signal', -.48, -1.03),
    # Cells; molecular structure; experimental manipulation; organisms.
    (r'cell|molecul|biolog|receptor|membran|apopt|prolif|cytoplasm', -.48, -.14),
    (r'residue|sequence|domain|subunit|isoform|terminal|affinit', -.51, -1.86),
    (r'knock(?:down|out)$|recombin|transfect|immunoblot|'
     r'immunoprecip|blot(?:$|ting)', -1.78, -1.69),
    (r'mouse|mice|yeast|strain|fibroblast|lymphocyt|neuron|human|mammal', -.39, -1.05),
)
RULES = tuple(re.compile('^(?:' + rule + ')') for rule, _, _ in FAMILIES)

@lru_cache(maxsize=30000)
def classify(word):
    return tuple(bool(rule.search(word)) for rule in RULES)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', '', '', 0., 0.)
    _, fragment, previous, before_previous, nearby, background = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    continuation = bool(fragment and token and token[0].isalpha())
    words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+', fragment + token if continuation else token)
    word = words[-1].lower() if words else ''
    hits = classify(word)
    f, b = min(1., nearby), min(1., background)
    value = -.007 - .13*f - .20*b
    value += sum(hit*(ordinary + b*extra)
                 for hit, (_, ordinary, extra) in zip(hits, FAMILIES))

    if word == 'of':
        value -= .2*f + .4*b
        preceding = classify(previous)
        if preceding[3] or (previous in {'level','levels'} and classify(before_previous)[3]):
            value -= 2.8 + 2.14*b
        elif preceding[4]:
            value -= .71 + .62*b
        elif preceding[5]:
            value -= 1.41 + .89*b
        elif preceding[7]:
            value -= .61 + .25*b
    elif word == 'that':
        value += -.03 + .12*f - .68*b
    elif word in {'in','to','for','with','by','from','against'}:
        value -= .45*f + .05*b
    elif word in {'the','a','an'}:
        value -= .07*b
    elif word in {'and','or'}:
        value -= .09*f + .12*b
    elif word in {'is','are','was','were'}:
        value += .17*f + .16*b

    if word in {'line','lines'} and previous in {'cell','cells'}:
        value -= 2.58
    if word == 'type' and previous == 'wild':
        value -= 1.25
    for group, strength in (
        ({'level','levels'}, 1.52), ({'function','functional'}, 1.13),
        ({'activity','activities'}, 1.95), ({'anti'}, 3.15),
        ({'tag','tagged'}, 1.29), ({'knock'}, 1.78),
    ):
        if word in group:
            value -= strength*b

    cue = float(any(hits[:3]) or hits[6])
    if word.startswith(('transfect','recombin','immunoblot','immunoprecip')):
        cue = 1.
    nearby = min(2., .7*nearby + .7*cue)
    background = min(2., .99*background + .5*cue)
    fragment = words[-1] if token and token[-1].isalpha() and words else ''
    return (doc, fragment, word, previous, nearby, background), float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP neuron 5128 (the down_proj component), as a readable rule.

What it does: this component is near zero on most text, and goes negative in
molecular-biology research prose. Its largest negative values fall on the word
"expression" in the gene/protein sense ("enhanced expression of ..."), and on the
preposition "of" (or "that", "for") right after a biology process noun: "expression of",
"induction of", "binding of", "activity of", "levels of", "role of". Plain biology
words (protein, gene, cells, domain, ...) are mildly negative on their own. The whole
pattern is stronger the more biological the surrounding text has been, and the first
token of a document sits slightly negative.

Per document the program keeps a decaying count of molecular-biology words (BIO), a
topic signal. At each token it adds up these pulls toward negative:
  1. the word itself: a process noun or a plain biology word, scaled up by BIO;
  2. a function word ("of", "that", "for", ...) right after a process noun, scaled by BIO;
  3. a small pull on function words in biology text, scaled by BIO;
  4. a small pull on the first token of each document.
"""

READS = ()

FUNCTION_WORDS = set("of that for the in to a an or and with its".split())

# Process nouns: a following "of"/"that" goes strongly negative; the word itself too.
PROCESS_NOUNS = {
    "expression": 1.0, "expressions": 0.8, "overexpression": 0.9, "knockdown": 0.8,
    "induction": 0.7, "binding": 0.6, "inhibition": 0.6, "activity": 0.6, "activities": 0.5,
    "activation": 0.6, "phosphorylation": 0.6, "disruption": 0.6, "levels": 0.5, "level": 0.3,
    "regulation": 0.5, "recruitment": 0.5, "involvement": 0.5, "inhibitors": 0.5,
    "inhibitor": 0.5, "signaling": 0.5, "signalling": 0.5, "transcription": 0.5,
    "depletion": 0.5, "deletion": 0.5, "secretion": 0.4, "mutation": 0.4, "mutations": 0.4,
    "role": 0.3, "synthesis": 0.3, "function": 0.3, "ulation": 0.5, "lation": 0.5,
}

# Other molecular-biology words: negative on their own, but they do not set up "of".
CONTENT_WORDS = {
    "protein": 0.3, "proteins": 0.3, "gene": 0.3, "genes": 0.3, "cells": 0.3, "cell": 0.3,
    "rna": 0.3, "mrna": 0.3, "dna": 0.3, "domain": 0.3, "domains": 0.3, "sequence": 0.3,
    "sequences": 0.3, "kinase": 0.3, "receptor": 0.3, "pathway": 0.3, "mutant": 0.3,
    "mutants": 0.3, "human": 0.3, "lines": 0.3, "residues": 0.3, "anti": 0.8,
}

# Words that mark molecular-biology text (they feed BIO, the topic signal).
BIO_WORDS = set(PROCESS_NOUNS) | set(CONTENT_WORDS) | {
    "expressed", "expressing", "knockout", "transfected", "recombinant", "plasmid",
    "antibody", "antibodies", "ligand", "enzyme", "enzymes", "polypeptide", "transcript",
    "mice", "mouse", "tissue", "tissues", "cultured", "culture", "regulated", "induced",
}

DECAY = 0.99
START_OF_DOCUMENT = -0.2


def _word(text):
    """The run of letters at the end of the token, lowercased ('' if it ends in a non-letter)."""
    out = ""
    for ch in text:
        out = out + ch.lower() if ch.isalpha() else ""
    return out


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if first:
        bio, prev_process = 0.0, 0.0
    else:
        _, bio, prev_process = carry
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = _word(text)
    token = text.strip().lower()
    process = PROCESS_NOUNS.get(word, 0.0)
    content = CONTENT_WORDS.get(word, 0.0)
    is_function = 1.0 if token in FUNCTION_WORDS else 0.0

    value = -(
        (process + content) * (0.9 + 0.5 * bio)
        + is_function * prev_process * (1.6 + 0.4 * bio)
        + is_function * 0.03 * bio
        + 0.04 * bio
    )
    if first:
        value = START_OF_DOCUMENT
    new_bio = bio * DECAY + (1.0 if word in BIO_WORDS else 0.0)
    return (doc, new_bio, process), value

"""Sparse responses to selected Chinese treasure, ruler and origin vocabulary.

The strongest negatives are 宝/寶 (treasure) and 帝 (emperor). Smaller
responses cover a few compounds, origins, secrets and curses. Treasure
characters split across UTF-8 tokens respond more strongly; 瑰宝 is weaker.
There are separate responses to document-opening code and middle-dot runs.
Everything else predicts zero. State resets at each new document.
"""
import codecs

READS = ()
# Beginning, ancestor, fundamental/root, and 'at the beginning'.
ORIGINS = {'始', '祖', '根本', '的根本', '之初'}
OCCULT = {'秘', '詛', '神器'}  # secret, curse, magical implement


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    pending, previous = (b'', '') if first else carry[1:3]
    raw = pending + prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    text, used = codecs.utf_8_decode(raw, 'ignore', False)
    word = text.strip()
    dot_run = text == '··' and (first or carry[3])
    carry = (doc, raw[used:], text, dot_run)
    simple = word.replace('寶', '宝')

    value = 0.0
    if simple == '宝':
        value = -10.0 if pending else -6.2
        if previous.endswith('瑰'):
            value = -2.7
    elif word == '玉' and pending:  # jade, with a split spelling
        value = -2.8
    elif simple in {'宝宝', '宝贝'}:  # baby / darling
        value = -2.6
    elif simple in {'法宝', '宝藏'}:  # magical treasure / hoard
        value = -1.8
    elif word == '帝':
        value = -4.6
    elif word in {'皇帝', '上帝'}:  # emperor / God
        value = -1.8
    elif word in ORIGINS or word == '本事':  # ability
        value = -1.2
    elif word in OCCULT:
        value = -1.5
    elif text == '··':
        value = 2.03 if dot_run else 0.24
    elif first and text == 'using':
        value = -2.46
    elif first and text in ('`', '("', "('"):
        value = -1.3
    return carry, value

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5129 (a sparse, mostly negative, token-specific feature).

It is silent on nearly all text. It goes strongly negative on the single-character
Chinese tokens 宝 and 寶 ("treasure") and 帝 ("emperor"), and more weakly on a few
related words: 皇帝, 上帝 (emperor), 宝贝, 宝宝, 宝玉, 法宝, 宝藏 (treasure), and 秘
(secret), 始 (begin), 初始 (initial), 根本 (fundamental), 本事 (ability). It is
also negative on the token 'using' when it opens a document right after <|endoftext|>.
On the middle-dot token '··' it is mildly positive, growing with the length of an
unbroken run of such tokens (degenerate repetition), and large inside long runs.

This program writes those values and nothing else: 0 everywhere, so its predictions
explain the large events and miss the small noisy fluctuations of common tokens.
"""

# Values are typical activations of each word, measured on training text.
TREASURE = {"宝": -6.4, "寶": -6.2, "宝贝": -2.4, "宝宝": -2.5, "宝玉": -1.8, "法宝": -1.5, "宝藏": -2.0}
EMPEROR = {"帝": -4.9, "皇帝": -2.1, "上帝": -2.0}
OTHER = {"秘": -1.5, "始": -1.5, "初始": -1.5, "根本": -1.4, "本事": -1.4}
TABLE = {**TREASURE, **EMPEROR, **OTHER}
READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """carry = length of the current run of '··' tokens (reset at each new document)."""
    run = 0
    if carry is not None and prefix.position > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-1] == prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        run = carry
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if tok == "··":
        run += 1
        value = 2.0 if run >= 50 else 0.3
        return run, value
    value = TABLE.get(tok, 0.0)
    if tok == "using" and prefix.position > 0 and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "<|endoftext|>":
        value = -2.4
    return 0, float(value)

r"""Escape-marker detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj, component 5130 (layer 1).

Plain-terms summary
- The component reads backslash escapes in text. It is positive on the escape marker of
  an escaped string, and negative on a LaTeX row break.
- A token with two or more backslashes (`\\`, `\\\\`) is the escape marker:
  * inside escaped code, i.e. the recent text already has escaped quotes (`\"`), as in
    code strings or JSON tool calls, it is positive (about +3);
  * in LaTeX math, where the recent text has two or more LaTeX commands (\\frac, \\left,
    \\begin, ...), it is a matrix or array row break and is negative (about -4);
  * otherwise it is mildly positive (+3).
- An escaped quote `\"` that directly follows a lone backslash token is strongly
  positive (+7): the second half of a doubly escaped quote.
- An asterisk right after a lone backslash (a markdown escape `\*`) is positive (+4).
- Everything else, including ordinary text and `\n` or `\t` escapes, is 0.

The rule only looks at the text before the token (the last 200 characters of the
current document), so it can be run one token at a time. Its value is what the
component's activation is predicted to be at that token.
"""

READS = ()
WINDOW = 200
LATEX_COMMANDS = (
    "\\frac", "\\left", "\\right", "\\begin", "\\end", "\\text", "\\mathrm", "\\hfill",
    "\\sum", "\\lim", "\\alpha", "\\sqrt", "\\cdot", "\\times", "\\color", "\\phantom",
    "\\quad", "\\displaystyle", "\\mathbb", "\\pmatrix", "\\array", "\\over",
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = carry if (same_doc and carry is not None) else ""
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    marks = tok.count("\\")
    value = 0.0
    if marks >= 2:
        latex = sum(before.count(cmd) for cmd in LATEX_COMMANDS) >= 2
        escaped_code = '\\"' in before
        value = -4.0 if (latex and not escaped_code) else 3.0
    elif marks == 0 and tok.startswith("*") and prev.endswith("\\"):
        value = 4.2
    elif marks == 1 and '"' in tok and prev.endswith("\\"):
        value = 7.0
    return (before + tok)[-WINDOW:], value

"""Approximate a lexical-unit completion signal, strongest for technical terms.

Pulse at the end of a WordNet noun compound, with larger pulses for credit,
real-property and telephone terms. A small supplementary vocabulary covers
modern technical collocations and software names. Other positions get zero,
apart from a negative pulse on the first token of each document. Continuations
inside a compound's last word get a reduced pulse. C# and C++ get strong
pulses. Only a short text suffix is carried and reset at document boundaries.
This does not model the substantial differences between individual dictionary compounds.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()

TECHNICAL_COLLOCATIONS = frozenset(
    'machine learning|deep learning|cloud computing|edge computing|'
    'big data|data analytics|supply chain|signal processing|'
    'social networking|social network|social media|project management|'
    'human resources|web designer|web design|web development|source code|'
    'batch size|risk factor|criminal justice|electric vehicle|'
    'best practices|smart city|quantum computing'.split('|')
)
LANGUAGES = frozenset(
    'python java javascript typescript rust julia fortran cobol haskell '
    'scala kotlin swift golang matlab perl ruby php lua sql postgresql '
    'mysql bash powershell'.split()
)
SOFTWARE_LIBRARIES = frozenset(
    'numpy scipy pandas matplotlib tensorflow pytorch keras torchaudio '
    'sklearn sympy pytest tkinter openmp jboss hamcrest junit phpunit '
    'symfony laravel django flask jquery lodash'.split()
)
FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    'a an the of and for in on at to by with from as is was be are have '
    'it that this his her your their our some its'.split()
)


@lru_cache(maxsize=30000)
def compound_strength(phrase):
    if any(w in FUNCTION_WORDS for w in phrase.split()):
        return 0.0
    # WordNet spells some compounds, such as cellphone, without spaces.
    forms = (phrase, phrase.replace(' ', ''))
    cats = wordnet.categories(phrase)
    if not cats:
        return 0.0
    if wordnet.is_a(phrase, 'credit'):
        return 2.7
    if wordnet.is_a(phrase, 'real property'):
        return 1.5
    if any(wordnet.is_a(f, 'telephone') for f in forms):
        return 1.7
    if not any(c.startswith('noun.') for c in cats):
        return 0.0
    if 'noun.possession' in cats:
        return 0.75
    if 'noun.substance' in cats:
        return 0.60
    return 0.42


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tail = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = (tail + token)[-100:]
    value = 0.0
    if re.search(r'[A-Za-z]$', text) and re.search(r'[A-Za-z]', token):
        words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+|[^A-Za-z\s]+', text.lower())
        for n in (2, 3):
            if len(words) >= n and all(w.isalpha() for w in words[-n:]):
                phrase = ' '.join(words[-n:])
                value = max(value, compound_strength(phrase))
        if tail[-1:].isalpha() and token[:1].isalpha():
            value *= 0.3
        if len(words) >= 2 and ' '.join(words[-2:]) in TECHNICAL_COLLOCATIONS:
            value = 2.0
        if words[-1] in LANGUAGES:
            value = 0.3
        if words[-1] in SOFTWARE_LIBRARIES:
            value = 0.5
    if '#' in token and re.search(r'\b[Cc]#\s*$', text):
        value = 2.35
    elif '+' in token and re.search(r'\b[Cc]\+\+\s*$', text):

right after a t and the o is followed by a consonant: "phot|oc|urrent", "dapt|om|ycin",

U_LETTERS = set("uUуУüÜúÚùÙ")            # u, Cyrillic у, accented u
O_LETTERS = set("oOоОοö")               # o, Cyrillic о, Greek ο, ö
SYLLABLE_NEXT = set("aeiosyzAEIOSYZ")   # a vowel (or s) right after the u
WEAK_NEXT = set("rpnlRPNL")             # r, p, n, l right after the u

    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]

What it does, in plain terms:
  Its activation is almost always near zero (typical size 0.05). Its rare large
  values are idiosyncratic: strongly negative on the token that follows some
  "after / back / post / not"-type words (后, 後, 先, post, back, not ...) and on

  these concepts carries much of its variance on held-out text.

  document (the first token after a document break, which is where the model
  resets attention): there the activation is on average slightly negative
  (about -0.08), while everywhere else it is about zero.

baseline, not an explanation of the component's large activations.

DOC_START_MEAN = -0.08


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # A new document starts at position 0 of a row and wherever the document id changes.
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]:
        return None, DOC_START_MEAN
    return None, 0.0

    """Print the prediction for a short example text: the first token gets -0.08."""
    tokens = ["The", " cat", " sat"]

1. Start of a document (its first token, including the first token of each row): the
   value is a fixed function of that token, since no earlier context exists. Coarse
   classes: special tokens (+0.18), digits (-0.10), words and spaces (-0.45), other
   symbols (-0.21).
2. The third digit of a year written after a month name, as in "25 Mar 2019": the '1' of
   "201" goes strongly negative (-0.55 on average).
3. A newline right after a run of at least five Title Case words (keyword-stuffed
   title lists, e.g. "Surface Area Of Square Pyramid Worksheets"): positive (+1.0).

token-specific noise that no short concept captures, so this explains about a tenth of it.

READS = ()

MONTH = re.compile(r"(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]*\b")


def start_value(token):
    """The activation at a document's first token, by its kind."""
    if "<|" in token:
        return 0.18
    if token[:1].isdigit():
        return -0.10
    if token[:1].isalpha() or token[:1] == " ":
        return -0.45
    return -0.21

    """carry: the document's text so far (last 60 characters), reset at each document start."""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        return "", start_value(token)
    before = carry or ""
    recent = before + token
    if token == "1" and recent[-3:-1] == "20" and MONTH.search(recent[-16:-2]):
        return recent[-60:], -0.55
    if "\n" in token:
        words = re.findall(r"\S+", before)[-6:]
        if len(words) >= 5 and all(w[0].isupper() and w.isalpha() for w in words):
            return recent[-60:], 1.0
    return recent[-60:], 0.0

The component turns negative on the word "test" (and its capitalised, path and
identifier forms: test, Test, TEST, /test, .test, Test::). It is strongest when
the word is a path or identifier piece (after "/", ":", "::", a quote), weaker
when it stands alone as a name, and near zero when it is English prose
("to test", "the test") or sits inside a longer word ("stdfRecTest").
Everything else predicts 0.

Values are the mean activation per class, fitted on 1024 training rows.
"""
READS = ()

TEST_WORDS = ("test", "Test", "TEST")
PLURAL_WORDS = ("tests", "Tests", "Testing", "testing")
PATH_END = ("/", ":", '"', "'")

# mean activation per class, fitted on training text
PATH_VALUE = -1.65      # "/test", "::Test", '"test': a path or identifier piece
NAME_VALUE = -0.9       # a standalone "Test" / " test" used as a name
PROSE_VALUE = -0.15     # "to test", or "test" glued into a longer word
PLURAL_VALUE = -0.15    # "tests", "Testing"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    core = tok.lstrip(" ./_")
    if core in PLURAL_WORDS:
        return None, PLURAL_VALUE
    if core not in TEST_WORDS:
        return None, 0.0
    glued = prev[-1:].isalpha() and tok[:1] not in " ./"
    prose = tok[:1] == " " and core == "test" and prev[-1:].isalpha()

    if prev.endswith(PATH_END):

    return None, NAME_VALUE

"""Finance-word detector (layers.1.mlp.down_proj component 5157).

This component writes a strong "this is a finance word" signal into the residual stream.
It is quiet on almost all text and spikes on the token where a word meaning *finance* or
*financial* is being spelled out or named, in English and in other languages:

  - English: "fin" + "ance"/"ancial" pieces, and whole words such as " finance",
    " Financial", " financing", " finances", "fiscal" (moderate).
  - Scandinavian / German / Polish-style "finans", "finanz" (the completing piece is the
    strongest signal of all).
  - Russian "фин" + "анс" / "финанс".
  - Chinese / Japanese 財 and 财 (wealth, finance; 财务, 财经, 财政 ...), Vietnamese "tài"
    (tài chính), Korean 재 (재정).

Words that merely look similar, such as "find", "final", "define", "fine", or "finger", do
not fire, and neither does Chinese 金融 ("finance"), which is slightly negative.

The program tracks the word being typed (letters since the last non-letter, reset at a
new document) and reads its activation off a small lexicon of finance words. The values
are typical activations for each word, in the component's own units.

Main idea: predict the activation as the lexicon value of the current word, else 0.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Whole words (lowercase) and the activation typically seen at the token that completes them.
FINANCE_WORDS = {
    "finans": 12.0,
    "finanz": 9.0,
    "finance": 4.5,
    "financing": 2.7,
    "finances": 2.3,
    "financial": 2.0,
    "финанс": 3.5,
    "fin": 1.0,
    "fiscal": 0.9,
    "фин": 0.8,
}

# Word beginnings that are finance words in most spellings, e.g. "financ", "finan".
FINANCE_STEMS = (("financ", 2.5), ("finan", 2.0), ("финан", 2.5))

# Single characters or syllables that mean wealth/finance, and their typical activations.
FINANCE_CHARS = {"財": 9.0, "财": 5.0}
# Syllables that are finance words only when they are the whole token (재 alone, tài alone).
FINANCE_TOKENS = {"재": 4.5, "tài": 7.0}

LETTER_RUN = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]+$")  # trailing letters of a token, Unicode-aware


def _word_value(word, token):
    if word in FINANCE_WORDS:
        return FINANCE_WORDS[word]
    for stem, value in FINANCE_STEMS:
        if word.startswith(stem):
            return value
    return 0.0


def _char_value(token):
    value = FINANCE_TOKENS.get(token.strip(), 0.0)
    for char, strength in FINANCE_CHARS.items():
        if char in token:
            value = max(value, strength)
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at this position: the finance-word lexicon value of the word being typed."""
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    word = "" if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()
    tail = LETTER_RUN.search(token)
    tail = tail.group(0) if tail else ""
    # A token made only of letters, with no leading space, continues the current word.
    if tail and tail == token and word:
        word = word + tail
    else:
        word = tail
    value = max(_word_value(word, token), _char_value(token))
    return word, value

"""A coarse approximation with document-initial and broken-prose modes.

Initial tokens use length, case, spacing, formatting, and article/preposition
membership as weak baselines. A lone initial tab has a large positive value.
Later, punctuation ending in a period or exclamation mark gets a larger
prediction when recent prose repeatedly terminates after function words.
A dangling function word plus a recent exclamation/ellipsis can also trigger
this rule. Newlines suppress it; function-word density scales its strength.
Most other positions get near zero. These surface rules leave much lexical
variation unexplained. The bounded text tail resets at document boundaries.
"""
import re
import unicodedata

READS = ()
ARTICLES = frozenset('a an the'.split())
PREPOSITIONS = frozenset('''
of to in on at for from by with into onto over under through between among
within without about against toward towards upon as
'''.split())
OPEN_ENDED = ARTICLES | PREPOSITIONS | frozenset('''
and or but nor yet although because if while than whether that
is are was were be been being has have had do does did will would
can could should shall may might must
all any some each every no many much more most few several
'''.split())
BROKEN_END = re.compile(
    r'\b(?:' + '|'.join(sorted(OPEN_ENDED)) + r')[.!?]'
)
LAST_WORD = re.compile(r'([a-z]+)$')


def initial_value(token):
    """Coarse first-token baselines; no lexical token lookup."""
    if token == '\t':
        return 2.05
    if token == ' ':
        return 0.33
    if token == '<|im_start|>':
        return -0.25
    word = token.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    punctuation = bool(word) and all(
        unicodedata.category(c).startswith('P') for c in word
    )
    # At a document's start, short pieces and formatting generally have
    # positive offsets; longer words and leading blanks lower the estimate.
    value = -0.028 - 0.018 * min(len(word), 15)
    value -= 0.119 * token.startswith(' ')
    value += 0.359 * token.isspace()
    value += 0.043 * word.isupper() + 0.062 * word.istitle()
    value += 0.116 * word.islower() + 0.169 * word.isdigit()
    value += 0.177 * punctuation
    value += 0.297 * word.startswith('#')
    value += 0.236 * word.startswith('.')
    value -= 0.110 * word.startswith('<|')
    value += 0.093 * (len(word) == 1 and word.isalpha())
    value += 0.120 * (lower in ARTICLES)
    value += 0.131 * (lower in PREPOSITIONS)
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        text = ''
        first = True
    else:
        text = carry[1]
        first = False
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.002
    if first:
        value = initial_value(token)
    elif token and all(c in '.,:;!?' for c in token) and token[-1] in '.!':
        recent = text[-350:].lower()
        older = text.lower()
        match = LAST_WORD.search(older)
        dangling = bool(match and match[1] in OPEN_ENDED)
        broken = len(BROKEN_END.findall(older))
        repeated = '!' in recent or '...' in recent
        if '\n' not in recent and (
            broken >= 2 or (dangling and repeated)
        ):
            words = re.findall(r'[a-z]+', older[-500:])
            ratio = sum(w in OPEN_ENDED for w in words) / max(1, len(words))
            strength = min(1.0, max(0.25, (ratio - 0.15) / 0.20))
            if '!' in token:
                value = 1.0 if dangling else 0.65
            elif '..' in token:
                value = 0.65 if dangling else 0.50
            else:
                value = 0.25 if dangling else 0.10
            value *= strength
        else:
            value = 0.005
    return (document, (text + token)[-750:]), value

"""Where a document starts, and stand-in punctuation in the middle of prose.

Two readable regularities, both small in size:

1. First token of a document (position 0 of a packed row, or the first token
   after an <|endoftext|> boundary). The component reads the token's kind:
   an indent tab writes strongly (about 2), other non-letter tokens (digits,
   punctuation, spaces, newlines) write a little (0.2), special tokens write a
   little negative (-0.25), and ordinary word-initial tokens stay near 0.

2. An exclamation mark or ellipsis used as a stand-in for a missing word or
   formula, i.e. right after an article or preposition ("the !", "of ...",
   "to !"). That is where the component fires (about 0.5 on average, up to ~2).
   Sentence-final exclamations ("Good!", "Perfect!") stay near 0.

Everything else is predicted as 0. The component's activation is otherwise a
small, token-specific wobble (sd about 0.04) that no short rule captures.
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

INDENT_TAB = 2.0
DOC_START_NON_LETTER = 0.2
DOC_START_SPECIAL = -0.25
STAND_INS = {"!", "...", "....", ".!"}
NOUN_SLOT_WORDS = {" a", " an", " the", " of", " to", " in", " for", " as", " by", " with", " on", " at", " from"}
STAND_IN_LEVEL = 0.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        if tok == "\t":
            return carry, INDENT_TAB
        if tok.startswith("<|"):
            return carry, DOC_START_SPECIAL
        if not any(ch.isalpha() for ch in tok):
            return carry, DOC_START_NON_LETTER
        return carry, 0.0
    if tok in STAND_INS and prefix.token_strings[-2] in NOUN_SLOT_WORDS:
        return carry, STAND_IN_LEVEL
    return carry, 0.0

"""A familiarity signal for repeated, tightly associated token pairs.

Count spellings and neighboring pairs within each document, ignoring case
and edge spaces. Strong association predicts negative activation, especially
for joined alphabetic pieces. Common English spellings get a weaker response.
Tokens without letters or numbers stay near zero. New pairs get only a small
class-specific baseline. These are count-based rules, not semantic lookups.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
from math import log1p, sqrt
import regex
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()

# Baseline, ending specificity, two-way association, log repetition count.
SCALES = (
    (0.031, 0.066, -0.169, -0.073),    # other mixed spellings
    (-0.020, -0.454, -0.647, -0.061),  # Latin-bearing tokens
    (-0.077, -0.270, -0.778, -0.428),  # joined Latin letters
    (-0.032, -0.174, 0.074, -0.407),   # other alphabetic tokens
    (-0.035, -0.080, -0.944, -0.487),  # joined non-Latin letters
    (0.016, -0.066, -0.544, 0.053),    # digits
)


@lru_cache(100000)
def spelling_properties(raw):
    word = raw.strip()
    latin = bool(regex.search(r'\p{Script=Latin}', word))
    frequency = zipf_frequency(word, 'en') if word else 0.0
    return latin, frequency


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    token = raw.strip().lower()
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        carry = (document, {}, {}, '', '')
    _, counts, pairs, prev, prevraw = carry
    pair = (prev, token)
    count = counts.get(token, 0)
    repeats = pairs.get(pair, 0)

    if not any(ch.isalnum() for ch in raw):
        value = 0.02
    else:
        ending_match = sqrt(repeats / max(count, 1))
        neighbor_match = repeats / max(counts.get(prev, 0), 1)
        joined = bool(raw and prevraw and raw[0].isalpha()
                      and prevraw[-1].isalpha())
        latin, frequency = spelling_properties(raw)
        if token.isdigit():
            kind = 5
        elif latin:
            kind = 2 if joined else 1
        elif joined:
            kind = 4
        elif token.isalpha():
            kind = 3
        else:
            kind = 0
        salience = 1.0
        if kind == 1:
            salience = max(0.0, min(1.0, (6.5 - frequency) / 1.7))
        match = ending_match * salience
        features = (1.0, match, match * neighbor_match,
                    match * log1p(min(repeats, 30)))
        value = sum(w * x for w, x in zip(SCALES[kind], features))

    counts[token] = count + 1
    pairs[pair] = repeats + 1
    return (document, counts, pairs, token, raw), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5159 as a "copying a repeated multi-token word" detector.

What it does: this component goes strongly negative when the current token continues a
word, name or phrase that has already appeared earlier in the same document, and the
preceding tokens also repeat that earlier stretch (e.g. the second "ino" in "httpPino"
the second time it is written, or "Richardson" after "Dr.", seen again). It stays near 0
on first occurrences and on ordinary text.

How: for each token, look back at earlier occurrences of the same token in the document
and measure how many preceding tokens also match (up to 8). Strength is then set by the
kind of token: an alphabetic word fragment with no leading space is strongest (it is
the middle or end of a split word), a spaced word is medium, and punctuation or other
tokens are weak. Repeating only the single token (match length 1) gives nothing.

The numbers are the mean activation per (token kind, match length) group, measured on
training rows. Context is reset at each document boundary, as the model does.
"""

READS = ()
MAX_BACK = 8   # how far back to compare the repeated stretch
MAX_OCC = 20   # how many earlier occurrences of the token to check

# activation by match length 0..3+ for each token kind
FRAGMENT = (0.0, 0.0, -0.8, -1.05)   # alphabetic, no leading space: inside a split word
SPACED_WORD = (0.0, 0.0, -0.3, -0.5)  # alphabetic word with a leading space
OTHER = (0.0, 0.0, -0.06, -0.15)      # punctuation, digits, symbols


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "ids": [], "occ": {}}
    ids, occ = carry["ids"], carry["occ"]
    t = len(ids)
    best = 0
    for s in occ.get(tok, [])[-MAX_OCC:]:
        m = 1
        while m <= MAX_BACK and s - m >= 0 and ids[s - m] == ids[t - m]:
            m += 1
        best = max(best, m)
    ids.append(tok)
    occ.setdefault(tok, []).append(t)
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if s.strip().isalpha() and not s.startswith(" "):
        table = FRAGMENT
    elif s.strip().isalpha():
        table = SPACED_WORD
    else:
        table = OTHER
    return carry, table[min(best, 3)]

  base strength: sentence punctuation (. ! ? and 。！？) or a word/digit gives 0.5; other

- The strength rises with the number of words on the line (square-root ramp, full at three
  words), so bare breaks are silent and one-word lines are weak.
- A line containing code-like symbols is damped to 0.7 of its value.
- A newline right after a chat-template marker (<think>, </think>, <|im_end|>, ...) gives 0.
- A line of more than 100 tokens gives 0.
- A run of tabs at the start of a line (code indentation) gives 0.3.
- Every other token gives 0.

    # carry: (words so far on this line, has code symbol, tokens so far on this line)

        return (words, code, length + 1), 0.3

"""Estimate a negative line-ending signal for space-padded, columnar text.

Keep the current line, ignoring indentation when measuring inter-column gaps.
Punctuation attached to a newline changes the strength of that signal. Literal
backslash-n escapes count as line breaks too. Ordinary tokens are nearly zero.
Small separate rules cover document openings, title-label colons, and repeated
middle-dot leaders.
"""
import math
import re

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', '', 0)
    _, line, previous, position = carry
    position += 1
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    token = raw
    if token == 'n' and previous.endswith('\\'):
        line = line[:-1]
        token = '\n'
    token = token.replace('\\n', '\n')
    head = token.split('\n')[0]
    line += head
    value = -0.2 if position == 1 else 0.0

    if '\n' in token:
        punctuation = token.strip()
        gaps = [len(m.group()) for m in re.finditer(' {2,}', line)]
        interior = [len(m.group()) for m in
                    re.finditer(' {2,}', line.lstrip(' \t'))]
        padding = math.log1p(sum(interior))
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(' \t'))
        digits = sum(c.isdigit() for c in line)
        rulers = [len(m.group()) for m in
                  re.finditer(r'([-=_*#~])\1{2,}', line)]
        # Column-ending punctuation strengthens the response to padding;
        # an opening code brace instead weakens it.
        strength = (0.179 + 0.214 * (not punctuation)
                    + 0.505 * ('/' in punctuation)
                    + 0.700 * ('|' in punctuation)
                    + 1.058 * ('#' in punctuation)
                    - 0.161 * ('{' in punctuation))
        value = (-0.102 - strength * padding
                 - 0.0532 * min(10, max(rulers, default=0))
                 - 0.0575 * min(10, line.count('|'))
                 - 0.0392 * math.log1p(digits)
                 + 0.1612 * math.log1p(token.count('\n')))
        if '%' in punctuation:
            value -= 1.172 * math.log1p(len(gaps))
        if ')' in punctuation or ']' in punctuation:
            value += 0.0645 * math.log1p(indent)
        # Spaces fused into the newline token give an extra padding signal.
        if line.strip():
            value -= 0.04 * head.count(' ')
        value = max(-6.0, min(1.0, value))
        line = token.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]
    elif position == 2 and previous == 'Title' and raw == ':':
        value = 4.8
    elif len(raw.strip()) >= 2 and set(raw.strip()) == {'·'}:
        value = -0.6
    return (doc, line, token, position), float(value)

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5165 as a "line break ending a padded table row" detector.

What it does, in plain terms: the component goes negative on the newline that ends a line of
column-aligned text: a table row, a file listing, a block of fixed-width columns. The wider the
padding between the columns (runs of two or more spaces or tabs between words, or a pipe), and
the more table-like lines in a row, the more negative it gets. Ordinary prose and code line
ends are near zero. A few line endings that close table rows or listings (" |", "/", " +",
" \\", CRLF) are negative even without padding. Everything inside a line is predicted as 0.

The program keeps the current line and how many table-like lines came just before it, within
the same document. At each newline it predicts
    -0.035 * min(padding, 40) * min(table lines in a row, 2)  -  0.5 * [line ends a table row]
    -0.02 otherwise (a plain line end is slightly negative on average)
where padding is the total width of the column gaps in the line that just ended.

Main points: the padding and a table block explain most of the large negative values. A plain
rule "newline => negative" explains almost nothing, because most newlines are ordinary. On
about 5,000 sampled rows this program explains about a quarter of the variance; the rest is
spread over many small activations in ordinary text, and the exact identity of each line-end
token adds some more that is not modelled here.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# runs of two or more spaces or tabs sitting between two non-space characters: the column gaps
PADDING = re.compile(r"(?<=\S)(?: {2,}|\t+)(?=\S)")
# a line is table-like if it has such a gap or a pipe between words
TABLE_LIKE = re.compile(r"\S(?: {2,}|\t+)\S|\|")
# line endings that close a table row or a listing row, even without padding
ROW_ENDS = {" |\n", "/\n", " +\n", " \\\n", "\r\n"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["document"] != document:
        carry = {"document": document, "line": "", "run": 0}
    if "\n" not in token:
        carry["line"] += token
        return carry, 0.0

    line = carry["line"] + token.split("\n")[0]
    padding = sum(len(gap) for gap in PADDING.findall(line))
    table_like = TABLE_LIKE.search(line) is not None
    depth = min(carry["run"] + 1, 2) if table_like else 0
    value = -0.035 * min(padding, 40) * depth - (0.5 if token in ROW_ENDS else 0.02)
    new_carry = {
        "document": document,
        "line": token.split("\n")[-1],
        "run": carry["run"] + 1 if table_like else 0,
    }
    return new_carry, value

small activations after the first token are deliberately not represented.

    "b": -5.08,
    "c": -1.40,
    "d": 2.29,
    "e": -0.40,
    "f": 3.98,

- the token's first letter (lowercased): strongly negative for words starting with m,

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 5168: a detector for base64-encoded text and
for UTF-16 text.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Base64 runs. Base64 is a stretch of letters, digits, '+' and '/' with no spaces (an
  embedded image, key, or encoded blob). The component wakes up once such a run has lasted
  a while, and its activation grows with the run length (about 0.3 after 16 characters,
  0.6 after 32, 1.0 after 64, saturating near 1.4 by 128+). The count resets at each
  document boundary.
- UTF-16 text. When text is stored as UTF-16 and read as bytes, every ASCII character is
  followed by a NUL byte, shown as the token '\\x00'. Those NUL tokens, inside a run of
  such text, get a large activation of about 2.

Everything else is predicted as 0. The component's real activation also has large
values on the first token of each document (no context, sign varies by token) and small
diffuse noise; this program does not model those.

Predictions are 0 unless one of the two patterns above is present.
"""

import math

READS = ()

# Characters that can appear in base64 text.
BASE64_CHARS = frozenset(
    "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/="
)
NUL_TOKEN = "\x00"          # the NUL byte, as a token, in UTF-16 text
NUL_VALUE = 2.0             # activation on NUL bytes inside UTF-16 text
TOP_VALUE = 1.3             # base64 run activation once the run is long (128+ chars)
MIN_RUN = 16                # shorter base64 runs are treated as ordinary text


def base64_ramp(run):
    """Activation for a base64 run of `run` characters: 0 below MIN_RUN, rising with log2 of
    the length and reaching TOP_VALUE at 128 characters."""
    if run < MIN_RUN:
        return 0.0
    return TOP_VALUE * min(1.0, (math.log2(run) - 3) / 4)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the current base64 run length (characters in a row, in this document).
    run = 0 if carry is None else carry
    if len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        run = 0  # a new document (or row start) resets the run
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token == NUL_TOKEN:
        # NUL bytes inside an ongoing base64-like run are UTF-16 text.
        return run, (NUL_VALUE if run > 0 else 0.0)
    if token and set(token) <= BASE64_CHARS:
        run += 1
    else:
        run = 0
    return run, base64_ramp(run)

CODE = re.compile(r'\b(?:def|class|const|let|var|int|double|String|float|'
                  r'auto|bool|self|this|return|new|public|private|static|'
                  r'function|void|import)\b|[;{}]')


def binding_value(before, operator):
    text = before.replace('\\n', '\n').replace('\\t', '\t')
    line = text.split('\n')[-1]
    match = re.search(r'([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*(?:(?:\.|->|::)'
                      r'[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)*)\s*$', line)
    if not match:
        return -0.5 if operator == ':=' else 0.0
    lhs = match[1]
    name = re.split(r'\.|->|::', lhs)[-1]
    words = re.findall(r'\w+', line[:match.start()])
    parts = {s.lower() for s in re.findall(
        r'[A-Z]?[a-z]+|[A-Z]+(?![a-z])', name)}
    lead = line[:match.start()]
    member = '.' in lhs or '->' in lhs
    typed = bool(words and (words[-1].lower() in TYPES or
                 words[-1][0].isupper() or lead.rstrip().endswith('>')))

        typed = False
    repeated_type = bool(words and len(name) > 2 and
                         words[-1].lower().endswith(name.lower()))
    code = bool(CODE.search(text[-300:]))

    if not code and len(name) == 1 and not member:
        return 0.0

    value += 2.8 * member + 0.7 * ('_' in name)
    value += 0.2 * (name.isupper() and len(name) > 1)
    value += 0.35 * (name[:1].isupper() and not name.isupper())
    value += 1.2 * (member and name.isupper())
    value -= 0.8 * bool(line[:1].isspace()) + 0.25 * code
    value -= 2.6 * bool(parts & OUTCOMES) + 3.3 * bool(parts & ERRORS)
    value -= 0.35 * ('value' in parts) + 0.7 * typed
    value -= 1.5 * repeated_type
    value += 1.1 * bool(re.search(r'\bconst\b', lead))
    value -= 0.3 * bool(re.search(r'\b(?:let|var)\b', lead))
    value -= 0.4 * (operator == ':=')
    value -= 1.1 * (operator not in ('=', ':='))
    return value


def expression_value(word, after_equals, after_colon, after_return):
    if word == 'await':
        return -5.9 if after_equals else -4.0 if after_return else -2.2
    if word in ('function', 'lambda', 'async'):
        if after_equals:
            return {'function': 5.0, 'lambda': 4.2, 'async': 3.0}[word]
        if after_colon:
            return 3.1 if word == 'function' else 1.5 if word == 'lambda' else 0.0
    if word in ('self', 'this'):
        if after_equals:
            return -1.75 if word == 'self' else -1.1
        if after_return:
            return -1.8 if word == 'self' else -0.7
        return -0.15 if word == 'self' else 0.0
    if after_equals and word.isidentifier():
        if word in ('null', 'None', 'nil', 'true', 'false'):
            return 0.6
        if word not in ('new', 'np', 'pd'):

    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', None)
    _, history, pending = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    left = history.rstrip()
    after_equals = pending is not None
    after_colon = left.endswith(':')
    after_return = bool(re.search(r'\breturn$', left))
    value = expression_value(word, after_equals, after_colon, after_return)
    next_pending = None
    op = re.search(r'([+*/%.:&|^-]?=)', token)
    if op and not any(s in token for s in ('==', '!=', '<=', '>=', '=>')):
        value = binding_value(history + token[:op.start()], op[1])
        suffix = token[op.end():].strip()
        if suffix:
            if suffix in ('function', 'lambda', 'async', 'self', 'this', 'await'):
                value = expression_value(suffix, True, False, False)
            elif suffix[0] in '\"\'':
                value = 0.2
            else:
                value *= 0.65
        else:
            next_pending = value
    elif not word and pending is not None:
        value = 0.25 * pending
        next_pending = pending
    elif word == '=>':
        value = 0.4
    elif token == '{"':
        value = -0.27
    elif word == ':' and re.search(r'\bfor\s*\([^)]*$', left):
        value = -1.7
    history = (history + token)[-700:]
    return (doc, history, next_pending), float(value)
